heading: INT. FENN & SON UPHOLSTERY - REAR LOADING DOCK - NIGHT

units.text: INT. FENN & SON UPHOLSTERY - REAR LOADING DOCK - NIGHT
Bolts of fabric stacked to the rafters.
A single hanging bulb.
The roll-up door is half open to the rain.
LAZLO FENN, 50s, a heavy-set man in suspenders, counts bills at a workbench.
RAY OBUYA, 30s, in a leather jacket, leans against a stack of velvet, thumbing a lighter on and off.
It's short.
units.name: RAY

units.text: It isn't.
units.name: LAZLO

units.text: Count it again.
units.name: RAY

units.text: Lazlo does not look up.
He finishes the stack, squares the edges against the bench, and starts a second.
Your boss has a long memory. So do I.
units.name: LAZLO

units.text: My boss said four. That's three-eight.
units.name: RAY

units.text: It's four.
units.name: LAZLO

units.text: Ray pushes off the velvet and takes one step.
He is close enough now to see the sweat on the other man's collar.
Then why are you counting like a man who got robbed?
units.name: RAY

units.text: Because I'm careful.
units.name: LAZLO

units.text: You've been careful for twenty years and I never once saw you count twice.
units.name: RAY

units.text: Lazlo stops.
He lays both hands flat on the money.
Behind him, a roll of fabric slumps on its stand.
Who's behind the roll?
units.name: RAY

units.text: Nobody.
units.name: LAZLO

units.text: He's smaller than you. He's breathing too hard.
units.name: RAY

units.text: Ray. Let it go.
units.name: LAZLO

units.text: Ray draws a revolver from the small of his back and lowers it, slowly, toward the floor.
Come out of there and I won't ask where the other two hundred went.
units.name: RAY

units.text: The roll shifts.
A boy, thin, no more than sixteen, steps out into the light with a fistful of cash held against his chest.
